newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian rubber prices end up but demand weak.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian rubber prices end up but demand weak.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices maintained midday levels to end higher, but sentiment remained weak with no business reported by most trading houses.
"It was a quiet day on all accounts...I don't think anything was done," said a trader.
"It's been a long weekend for the overseas markets after Good Friday and Easter," said another trader. "Moreover, the month is ending, so it's natural for buyers to be sidelined."
At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted April RSS1 buyer at 298.50 cents ($1.20) a kg, unchanged from Thursday.
April SMR20 buyer was up half cent at 285.50.
Traders said the higher prices were quoted by the MRELB in an effort to reduce producers' costs.
The traders, however, said they expected prices to fall by a cent or two this week as demand was proving hard to come by.

Traders offered the SMR20 at 285 cents a kg, SMR CV at 352, SMR L at 332, SMR 5 at 292, SMR 10 at 286 and drum latex FOB at 236. The INRO five-day indicator was down to 228.70 Malaysian/Singaporean cents per kg on March 27, from 228.87 a day earlier. The daily indicator was unchanged at 228.25.
